column1: # FlightRadar24 aircraft-page availability, probed from a REAL LOGGED-OUT BROWSER SESSION.
# Retrieved 2026-08-24 (UTC) by Claude in Chrome, fetching each page same-origin from
# www.flightradar24.com so Cloudflare's bot check was not in the way.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Our scripted probe (recover_erased.js) records HTTP 403 from
# flightradar24.com for every aircraft in this investigation, and that 403 was read on this
# site as evidence that a page had been REMOVED. It is not. FlightRadar24 returns 403 to any
# unrelated control aircraft got the identical 403 from the identical script.
# In a browser, EVERY aircraft page in this investigation loads, HTTP 200, with its full
# identity block. NONE of them has been removed from FlightRadar24.
# rows      = flight-history rows the free tier rendered. FlightRadar24 shows the LAST 7 DAYS
#             to a logged-out visitor and paywalls everything older ("More than 7 days of X
#             history is available with an upgrade to Silver (90 days)..."). paywall=1 on
#             every single row below, subject and control alike.
# nodata    = the page printed "Sorry, but we could not find data for specified flight",
#             which for a private aircraft means IT HAS NOT FLOWN IN THE LAST 7 DAYS. The
#             unrelated control N1KE (a Nike Gulfstream) prints it too.
# kind      = SUBJECT (this investigation) or CONTROL (nothing to do with this case).
